lesson.summary: The essentials of the Welfare Avenue brand from the Brand Guides (2026): who we are, who we speak to, our personality, how we speak and how we look, then a hard knowledge check.

blocks.text: Our brand is how people recognize Welfare Avenue and how they feel when they meet us: in a post, a flyer, an email or a conversation at a serving. Everyone who represents Welfare Avenue carries it, so everyone learns it.
The **Brand Guides** (2026) are the source. This lesson covers the essentials; the guide has the details, page by page.
If you call it the wrong word, someone reading this gets the wrong image of what we do.

It has 15 questions: 10 on the essentials in this lesson and 5 on details that are only in the Brand Guides, so read the guide first (it is the first item in this avenue). The questions and answers are shuffled for every attempt, a wrong answer points you to the page to check rather than showing the answer, and you need 12 right to pass.

Welfare Avenue is a youth-powered non-profit dedicated to fighting food insecurity and poverty through direct community action, delivering meals and essential support directly to people where they are.

**Our vision:** a world without poverty, where all individuals have the necessities they require and the opportunities available to them, and a society where community engagement is a central value from a young age.
We are a youth-inspired community mobilization, active in Montreal and Toronto. Young leaders bring the energy and advocacy, and our doors are open to volunteers and partners of all generations.
Our four pillars

items.d: Consistent, coordinated food distribution that brings healthy meals to our unhoused neighbours, using the meal to build the trust that leads to long-term social reintegration.
Seasonal clothing, hygiene essentials and basic items, given directly to families and individuals facing economic hardship, always with respect and solidarity.
A professional conduit between the trust we build on the street and long-term housing, mental health and employment support across our partners.
Community pop-ups, creative arts and recreational sports that break down social barriers, restore hope and build belonging.

blocks.text: Where the brand is going

As Welfare Avenue grows, the brand grows with it. The brand evolution shifts us from a **food-focused non-profit** to a **broader community movement**: one that brings people together through action, connection and collective care. The goal is a more relevant, inclusive and recognizable brand that engages more people and amplifies our impact.
The guide describes four personas. Each one hears the same mission, said for them.

items.d: Olivier, 47, stands for the people we serve. Backgrounds differ, but many lost their stability to things outside their control and feel forgotten, judged and excluded. They look for support and a community that restores dignity and belonging. Speak with warmth, consistency and reassurance.

Sarah, 21, believes in social justice and wants to grow, learn and give, and to gain real professional skills. She is proud to see everyone face to face at Sunday servings. Make taking part feel meaningful, structured and empowering.
Non-profits, charities and student associations aligned with our mission. They bring expertise, space and people. We present Welfare Avenue as a bridge within the existing care ecosystem.
Local, medium to large organizations with corporate social responsibility goals, looking for a demonstrable social return. Speak in terms of scale, outcomes and professional credibility.

blocks.text: Example sentences for each audience are on page 34 of the guide, and what each persona needs is on pages 10 and 11.
An archetype is a personality. It shapes every decision, so we do not just convey a message: we embody a relationship. Ours is a blend of four.

items.d: Relevant, authentic and simple. Seeks belonging; values real connections and simplicity; fears exclusion and rejection.
Altruist and protector. Cares for and helps others, with compassion, security and responsibility.
Courage and determination. Wants to do the impossible and leave a legacy, through strength, overcoming challenges and leadership.
Seeks happiness and harmony, and values kindness, honesty and simple, genuine experiences.

blocks.text: The guide also places Welfare Avenue on ten personality sliders, from Traditional to Modern and from Serious to Fun. Look at page 8 to see where we sit: some of them may surprise you.
Warmth with purpose. The words we choose decide the picture people have of us and of the people we serve.

items: The people we serve, community, support
Support, dignity, connection, safety
Food as a starting point, refer, reintegrate
Youth-powered, professional, movement, future leaders
Collaborate, ecosystem, conduit, partnership
Impact, scalable, measurable, systemic change
The homeless, beneficiaries, people in need
Pity, saving people, feeling sorry
Feed people, hand out food, give away snacks
Student club, just volunteers, small project
We do everything, we are the only ones
Donate, buy groceries, help us figure it out

blocks.text: Why

items: **Lead with the person, not their circumstance.** Our language protects dignity and creates belonging.
**Solidarity, never pity.** We communicate solidarity and empowerment, never charity from a position of superiority.
**Food is our conduit.** The meal builds trust; the larger goal is connection, dignity and social reintegration.
**Youth is an asset.** We show energy and innovation with the discipline of a maturing organization.
**We complement, we do not compete.** Our role is to connect people with the right support.
**Outcomes, not inputs.** We talk about impact, which shows a credible organization built for growth.

blocks.text: The guide has none, but formal filings like our CRA forms use beneficiaries because it is the legal term there. Everywhere else, we say the people we serve.
One logo family, five colours and two typefaces, used the same way everywhere.
The logo

items.d: WELFARE AVENUE, stacked, with the E that moves in AVENUE. The default mark.
WEL FAR E, the compact version for small and square spaces (pages 23 and 24).
The logo with its descriptor line: **Building pathways in our community**.
items.alt: The Welfare Avenue logo with its descriptor line

blocks.text: The guide sets the logo’s breathing space, its minimum sizes, the backgrounds that work and the uses we avoid (pages 21 to 25). Check them before you place the logo on anything.
Our colours

items.d: A warm foundation where people come first.
Rooted in connection and trust.
Clarity, structure and reliability.
Optimism for what comes next.
Energy that moves people forward.
items.use: Accents, highlights, H2 and H3, extra text

blocks.text: Our typefaces

items.sample: We use food as a starting point to build trust, connect people with specialized support, and create pathways toward greater dignity and reintegration.
items.role: Body text, UI, captions and metadata

items: Follow the 1.414 size scale and the weights it sets, in every medium.
Never set body copy in Barlow Condensed.
Never stretch, condense or skew either typeface.
Never swap in look-alikes such as Times or Arial.

chapters.t: Doodles and the E that moves

blocks.text: Keep it human. Our doodles add warmth, movement and personality: they should feel like a human hand showing up in the system.

items.d: Imperfect lines keep the brand human and approachable.
Simple shapes bring emotion without over-explaining.
A touch of spontaneity reflects our youth-powered spirit.
Every doodle supports the message and never competes with it.
items.alt: A hand-drawn chain of gold hearts

blocks.text: Use doodles to **frame** important content, **accent** headlines, numbers and calls to action, **connect** ideas with lines and gestures, and **layer** them with type, imagery and colour. The guide lists four things never to do with them on page 37.
The E that moves

items.d: A typographic device that turns the E into a pathway for movement, connection and progress.
items.alt: The E that moves: an E with long extended bars

items.d: Start with the headline in Barlow Condensed and convert the text to outlines.
Select the E and drag its bars horizontally until they fit the layout.
Use the extended lines to create a sense of direction, connection or progression.

blocks.text: Where to use it, and where not to, is on page 40 of the guide, with examples like TOGETHER WE MOVE FORWARD.
You do not need to be a designer to get the brand right.

items.d: Logos, doodles, colours, fonts, profile pictures, meeting backgrounds, posters, printables and the E component are in Rebranding 2026, 01. Assets. Use those files rather than redrawing or screenshotting the logo.
Before you post, send or present, read your words against How we speak.
Breathing space, minimum size and background: pages 21 to 25 of the guide.
Not sure something is on brand? Ask the marketing team, who look after it.
The full guide, 44 pages
Logos, doodles, fonts, posters, printables and the E component

blocks.text: you can say our mission in your own words, use the right words for the people we serve, and place the logo, colours and type the way the guide sets them.

quiz.title: The brand knowledge check
quiz.intro: Ten questions cover the essentials in this lesson. Five test details that are only in the **Brand Guides**, so read the guide before you start.

questions.q: Which of these is our mission, as the Brand Guides word it?
a: Welfare Avenue is a youth-powered non-profit dedicated to fighting food insecurity and poverty through direct community action, delivering meals and essential support directly to people where they are.
Welfare Avenue is a student club that hands out food to people in need every other Sunday.
Welfare Avenue is a food bank that collects donations for families across Canada.
Welfare Avenue is a national charity that funds other food programs through grants.
questions.why: That is the mission on the Who we are page. The others use words we avoid (student club, hands out food, people in need) or describe an organization we are not.

questions.q: What does the brand evolution change?
a: It shifts us from a food-focused non-profit to a broader community movement that brings people together through action, connection and collective care.
It shifts us from a youth-powered movement to a traditional charity with a corporate look.
It narrows our focus to food only, so the message stays simple.
It gives us a new name so we can expand across Canada.
questions.why: The brand grows with the organization: from food-focused to a broader community movement, so it can engage more people and amplify our impact. Our name stays Welfare Avenue.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of our four institutional pillars?
a: Running emergency shelters
Dismantling social isolation
Integrating the care ecosystem
Dignified resource distribution
questions.why: The four pillars are food security mobilization, dignified resource distribution, integrating the care ecosystem and dismantling social isolation. Running shelters is not one of them: we build trust and connect people with partners for housing, mental health and employment support.

questions.q: Which four archetypes make up our brand personality?
a: The Everyman, the Caregiver, the Hero and the Innocent
The Rebel, the Magician, the Explorer and the Sage
The Ruler, the Creator, the Lover and the Jester
The Caregiver, the Ruler, the Sage and the Rebel
questions.why: The Everyman (belonging and real connection), the Caregiver (care for others), the Hero (courage and overcoming challenges) and the Innocent (kindness, honesty and genuine experiences).

questions.q: Which sentence follows how we speak?
a: Join a youth-powered movement connecting the people we serve with the support they need.
Our student club hands out food to the homeless every other Sunday.
Help us save people in need: donate today.
We do everything for the less fortunate, because no one else will.
questions.why: It leads with the person (the people we serve), calls us a youth-powered movement and shows our role as the connection to support. The others use words or ideas from the We don’t say column: student club, hand out food, the homeless, saving people, people in need, donate, we do everything, we are the only ones.

questions.q: In our language, what role does food play?
a: A starting point: the meal builds trust, and the larger goal is connection, dignity and social reintegration.
The whole mission: we feed people, and that is the job.
A giveaway that brings people to our events.
A fundraising tool: meals are how we attract donors.
questions.why: Food is our conduit. We say food as a starting point, refer and reintegrate, never feed people, hand out food or give away snacks.

questions.q: Which pairing of typefaces is right?
a: Barlow Condensed for headlines, titles and display; Space Grotesk for body text, UI, captions and metadata
Space Grotesk for headlines; Barlow Condensed for body text
Barlow Condensed for everything, so it stays consistent
Arial for headlines and Times for body text when the brand fonts are not installed
questions.why: Barlow Condensed is for headlines, titles and display; Space Grotesk for body text, UI, captions and metadata. Never set body copy in Barlow Condensed, and never swap in look-alikes like Times or Arial.

questions.q: What are our five brand colours called?
a: Dignity, Community, Ground, Possibility and Action
Hope, Growth, Earth, Dream and Energy
Cream, Forest, Charcoal, Lavender and Mustard
Trust, Care, Safety, Joy and Courage
questions.why: Dignity (#FFFAF2, the warm cream), Community (#103F39, the deep green), Ground (#1F201E, near-black), Possibility (#6F64AB, purple) and Action (#DCA527, gold). Each name says what the colour stands for.

questions.q: What is the descriptor line that sits under our logo?
a: Building pathways in our community
Together we move forward
Small acts, real impacts, better futures
Youth-powered, community-driven
questions.why: The logo with description reads Building pathways in our community. Together we move forward and Small acts, real impacts, better futures are headlines from the guide’s social media examples.

a: Adding warmth, movement and personality, with every doodle supporting the message rather than competing with it
Filling empty space so a design never looks bare
Replacing photos when we do not have any
Replacing the logo on social media posts
questions.why: Keep it human: doodles are hand-drawn, expressive, playful and purposeful. They frame, accent, connect and layer, and each one needs a reason to be there.

questions.q: On the guide’s personality sliders, where does Welfare Avenue sit between Young and Mature?
a: Leaning toward Mature
All the way to Young
Right in the middle
Leaning toward Young
questions.why: The Young to Mature dot sits two steps toward Mature, even though we are youth-powered. The only slider pushed all the way to one end is Luxurious to Popular, fully Popular.

questions.q: According to the Sponsors persona, what do sponsors fear?
a: Reputational risk and instability
Being asked for money too often
Their money going to overhead instead of programs
Having too little say in how programs run
questions.why: Sponsors are driven by corporate social responsibility goals and want a demonstrable social return. They fear reputational risk and instability, so they need a mature, structured partner.

questions.q: How much clear space does the guide ask for around the logo?
a: At least one E from the logo, on every side
The full height of the logo
One centimetre, whatever the logo’s size
None, as long as the logo is readable
questions.why: The breathing space is measured with the logo’s own E, marked x on page 21, on all four sides, so it grows and shrinks with the logo.

questions.q: Which of these does the guide show as an incorrect use of the logo?
a: Adding a Santa hat or another prop to the logo for a holiday post
The cream logo on the deep green (Community)
The cream secondary logo, WEL FAR E, on gold (Action)
The green logo on a calm, light area of a photo
questions.why: Props, low contrast, two-tone colours, outlines, rotation and busy photos are all under Incorrect applications. The other three are on the Correct applications page.

questions.q: Which of these is on the guide’s don’t list for the E that moves?
a: Using it on every headline
Using it for major headlines
Keeping the E clearly recognizable
Using it to suggest progression
questions.why: Do: use it for major headlines, keep the E recognizable, let the extension interact with the layout, and use it to suggest progression. Don’t: use it in body copy or small type, stretch the entire word, or use it on every headline.

guide_desc:
The Brand Guides (version 1, 2026) are the source for how Welfare Avenue looks and sounds: 44 pages, about 25 minutes. Read it closely. Five of the fifteen questions in the knowledge check come from details that are only in the guide.

What to look for:

- Who we are (pages 4 to 8): our mission, vision and positioning, the four pillars, the brand evolution and our personality.
- Our personas (pages 9 to 11): the four audiences we speak to, and what each one needs.
- Brand archetypes (pages 12 to 18): the four personalities behind the brand.
- Logo (pages 19 to 25): the primary and secondary logos, breathing space, minimum sizes, and correct and incorrect uses.
- Typography (pages 26 to 29) and the colour palette (pages 30 and 31).
- How we speak (pages 32 to 34): the words we use, the ones we avoid, and the message for each audience.
- Doodles (pages 35 to 37) and the E that moves (pages 38 to 40).
- How it comes together (pages 41 to 43): social posts and printed pieces.

The logos, doodles, colours, fonts, profile pictures, meeting backgrounds, posters, printables and the E component are in [Rebranding 2026, 01. Assets](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HqAE-FHO2HRPvzpjhz8aGJpZLAbjIH8y) on the shared drive.

Open it with your Welfare Avenue Google account. If the preview asks you to sign in or stays blank, use Open the document.

Done when: you have read every section, then take the lesson and its knowledge check (next in this avenue).
module7_add: Three Learning Avenues are required for everyone: Welfare Avenue foundations, Our brand and Using the Hub. The Our brand knowledge check is a hard one: its 15 questions come in a new order every attempt, a wrong answer points you to the page of the Brand Guides to check instead of showing the answer, and you see every answer once you pass (12 of 15).
